At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and excellent opportunities for growth and advancement. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. jobs.title: Director, Portfolio Management
jobs.description:
WHY JOIN US?

At AstraZeneca, we are dedicated to being a Great Place to Work, where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and unleash your entrepreneurial spirit. With an ambitious goal of delivering 20 new medicines by 2030, there is no better place to make a difference in medicine, for patients, and in society.

Join us on this exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare. Our inclusive culture champions diversity and collaboration, and we are always committed to lifelong learning, growth, and development. As part of our team, you'll contribute to groundbreaking advancements that will shape a healthier future for people everywhere. Be a catalyst for change at AstraZeneca, where your work will have a real impact on improving people's lives.

Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork by engaging face-to-face in our offices 3 days a week
. Our head office is purposely designed with collaboration in mind, providing space where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects.

About AISI

AstraZeneca AI for Science Innovation (AISI) is driving the convergence of artificial intelligence and life sciences at enterprise scale. AISI brings together data foundations, AI and machine-learning technology, strategic partnerships, process reinvention, and business-facing AI to accelerate drug discovery, development, and delivery. Success depends on connecting and scaling existing capabilities, promoting reuse, and translating innovation into measurable scientific, patient, and enterprise value.

The Opportunity

The Director, Portfolio Management will lead the design, governance, and continuous improvement of AISI's portfolio management capability across strategic initiatives, AI and data platforms, external partnerships, projects, suppliers, managed services, and operational investments. The role ensures that strategy is translated into an executable portfolio, investments and resources are directed to the highest-value opportunities, delivery performance is transparent, and financial and operational risk, and compliance governance are embedded throughout the portfolio lifecycle.

Operating at the intersection of AISI leadership, scientific and therapeutic-area stakeholders, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, HR, and external partners, the Director will establish scalable ways of working, strengthen evidence-based decision-making, and deliver outcomes through cross-functional teams and managed-service providers. The role sits within AISI Operations and reports to the Head of AISI Operations.

Scope And Core Accountabilities

Portfolio Strategy, Planning, and Governance

Translate AISI strategy and scientific priorities into an integrated portfolio of investments, initiatives, platforms, products, partnerships, and operational services.
Establish and continuously improve demand intake, assessment, value-based prioritization, funding, resource allocation, stage-gate review, delivery assurance, and benefits-realization processes.
Maintain an integrated portfolio view, identifying opportunities to stop, sequence, accelerate, consolidate, reuse, or scale initiatives as priorities and evidence evolve.
Lead portfolio governance forums and provide clear executive reporting on investment, demand, delivery health, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, capacity, financial performance, and expected value.
Develop standardized dashboards and management information that enable timely, transparent, evidence-based decisions without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Financial and Investment Management

Partner with Finance and senior leaders to manage long-term investment planning, business cases, budgets, forecasts, and Run and Change expenditure.
Oversee forecast-versus-budget analysis, variance management, accruals, cross-charges, resource recharges, purchase orders, and supplier-related financial commitments.
Ensure financial information is accurate, timely, transparent, and connected to portfolio priorities, delivery milestones, and benefits realization.
Define and track financial and non-financial value measures, including scientific impact, speed, adoption, reuse, risk reduction, productivity, and enterprise scalability.

Operating Model and Process Excellence

Design and evolve the portfolio operating model, decision rights, governance forums, escalation pathways, and RACI frameworks required to manage a complex, global portfolio.
Drive standardization, simplification, automation, and continuous improvement across portfolio, project, financial, supplier, contracting, resource, onboarding, and service-management processes.
Introduce fit-for-purpose Agile, Lean Portfolio Management, Design Thinking, incremental delivery, and hybrid governance practices where appropriate.
Ensure processes are practical, adopted, and supported by reliable data and fit-for-purpose tools, including ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, and portfolio or financial-management platforms.

Partnership, Contracting, and Supplier Governance

Provide end-to-end portfolio oversight of strategic alliances, AI and data partnerships, technology providers, suppliers, and managed services.
Partner with Legal, Procurement, Finance, Privacy, Information Security, and technical leaders across the contracting lifecycle, from intake, due diligence, term-sheet development, and negotiation through execution, performance review, renewal, and exit.
Implement supplier and partner governance through scorecards, service-level agreements, periodic business reviews, delivery-quality measures, commercial-health monitoring, risk mitigation, and value-for-money assessments.
Ensure partner commitments, dependencies, milestones, financial obligations, and benefits are integrated into portfolio planning and reporting.

Resource and Capacity Management

Lead resource and capacity-management practices across projects, products, platforms, partnerships, and operational services.
Oversee workforce planning, allocation, utilization, people recharges, onboarding, and prioritization of scarce scientific, AI, engineering, and portfolio-management capabilities.
Work with functional leaders to identify capability gaps, resolve constraints, improve onboarding, and align internal and external capacity with strategic priorities.

Risk, Compliance, and Delivery Assurance

Establish portfolio-level approaches to risk, issue, dependency, assumption, and decision management, ensuring material concerns are identified early, escalated appropriately, and managed through resolution.
Provide oversight of scope, schedule, cost, quality, benefits, adoption, operational readiness, and delivery performance across the portfolio.
Ensure portfolio activities and external arrangements comply with relevant pharmaceutical and technology requirements, including data governance, GDPR and privacy, information security, intellectual property, procurement, ethical, quality, and regulatory frameworks.
Anticipate and manage delivery underperformance, supplier failure, commercial disputes, IP complexity, changing priorities, financial pressure, data and technology dependencies, and regulatory constraints.

Stakeholder Engagement and Change Enablement

Build trusted relationships with AISI and Enterprise AI leaders, therapeutic and scientific areas, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, Legal, HR, Operations, and external partners.
Facilitate alignment on priorities, investment choices, delivery expectations, trade-offs, and accountabilities across a global matrix organization.
Communicate complex portfolio, financial, commercial, and delivery matters clearly to senior leaders and diverse stakeholder groups.
Champion adoption of portfolio standards, transparent governance, and collaborative delivery while preserving the speed and experimentation required for AI innovation.

Leadership

Lead and develop high-performing portfolio management, governance, and business-operations capabilities, directly and through matrix teams and managed-service providers.
Create a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer focus, continuous improvement, reuse, and measurable value delivery.
Set clear standards and build scalable capabilities from the ground up, enabling consistent ways of working across functions and geographies.
Contribute to AISI functional strategy and operating model evolution as the organization, technology landscape, and partnership ecosystem mature.

Essential

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor's degree in business, technology, finance, life sciences, project management, law, data science, or a related discipline; a Master's degree or equivalent extensive professional experience is preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience across portfolio management, program or project management, business operations, financial management, alliance or partnership management, supplier governance, contracting, or a related discipline in a complex global organization.
Demonstrated experience leading portfolio management and process-transformation initiatives, including demand intake, value-based prioritization, governance, investment planning, resource allocation, delivery assurance, and benefits realization.
Strong financial acumen, including business-case development, long-term planning, investment tracking, forecasting, budget management, accruals, variance analysis, cross-charges, purchase orders, and resource recharges.
Experience managing suppliers, strategic partners, external collaborations, or managed services, including contracts, service levels, performance, commercial risk, value for money, and issue resolution.
Experience designing and implementing operating models, decision rights, governance forums, processes, RACI frameworks, dashboards, and management information.
Proven success influencing senior leaders and delivering through cross-functional teams, matrix structures, third parties, and managed-service providers.
Ability to operate with limited direction in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and make sound decisions that balance scientific and strategic value, risk, cost, capacity, compliance, and delivery feasibility.
Exceptional written, verbal, influencing, relationship management, and organizational skills.

Desirable

Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, life sciences, or another highly regulated technology environment.
Working knowledge of AI and machine-learning ecosystems, data partnerships, cloud platforms, digital products, technology platforms, and platform-based delivery models.
Understanding of pharmaceutical research and development and how AI, data, platforms, and external partnerships create scientific and competitive advantage.
Experience establishing or scaling portfolio management, alliance management, PMO, or business-operations function.
Experience with Agile, Scrum, SAFe, Lean Portfolio Management, Waterfall, Design Thinking, or hybrid delivery approaches.
Experience with ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, and comparable portfolio, project, financial, procurement, or service-management tools.
Knowledge of data governance, privacy, information security, intellectual property, quality, regulatory compliance, and IT risk management.
Professional qualifications such as PMP, PRINCE2, MSP, Scrum, SAFe, or equivalent portfolio, program, commercial, or supplier-management credentials.

Leadership Capabilities

Strategic thinking: Connects scientific and enterprise strategy to investment choices, delivery priorities, and measurable value.
Enterprise perspective: Optimizes across the portfolio, promotes reuse and scalability, and avoids isolated solutions.
Execution discipline: Establishes clear governance and follows through to achieve reliable delivery and benefits realization.

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.

The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.

We can’t wait to get to know you!

The Vice President, Strategy leads the development and management of the strategy for EQ’s Personal Bank, which brings together EQ Bank and PC Financial across products, customer experience and loyalty. Reporting to the VP, Customer Growth, Loyalty & Franchise Value, the role turns strategy into clear priorities, OKRs and investment choices, and runs the planning, performance and business management rhythm for the EVP, Personal Banking and the Personal Banking Senior Leadership Team, including quarterly business reviews and executive and Board reporting. Working closely with the Value Office, the Program Delivery Office and Enterprise Strategy, the role helps the Personal Bank focus on the right priorities and deliver measurable outcomes.

Strategy

Lead the development and annual refresh of the 3-year Personal Banking strategy across products, customer experience and loyalty, working with the VP and the Personal Banking Senior Leadership Team
Act as a strategic thought partner to business and product leaders, translating insight into clear priorities that align to objectives and key results (OKRs) and measurable outcomes
Lead structured, fact-based analysis of priority strategic questions, such as growth and profitability trade-offs, customer and franchise opportunities, and competitive and market trends, drawing on Analytics and customer insights
Shape priority strategic initiatives from concept to fundable business case, in partnership with the Value Office
Partner with Enterprise Strategy & Corporate Development to assess new business opportunities for the Personal Bank, including partnerships and M&A
Ensure the strategy reflects customer growth and loyalty (PC Optimum) priorities, working with the leaders accountable for them

Planning & Performance Management

Lead the annual strategic planning cycle and the OKR process for Personal Banking, aligned with the Value Office’s financial plan and forecasts
Run the quarterly business review (QBR) to track performance of priorities and initiatives, and recommend where resources and investment should be reprioritized
Build and own reporting against Personal Banking OKRs and strategic initiatives, including tracking benefits against business case commitments
Run the intake and prioritization process for Personal Banking investments, including capital expenditure, using clear evaluation criteria, and bring recommendations to the Senior Leadership Team in partnership with the Value Office, Digital and the Program Delivery Office
Partner with the Program Delivery Office to translate strategic priorities into delivery sequencing, weigh demand against capacity across Personal Banking, Enterprise Technology and vendors, and surface risks, dependencies and trade-offs for executive decision

Business Management & Executive Reporting

Provide business management support to the EVP, Personal Banking and the Senior Leadership Team, including the cadence of management meetings, agendas, presentations and executive forums, and follow-through on decisions and actions
Prepare quarterly Board materials on strategic progress, key decisions and outlook, and monthly progress updates to business leaders, reinforcing transparency and accountability
Coordinate Personal Banking input to enterprise strategy, executive and investor materials (for example, Investor Day)

About The Role

The Director of FP&A will own how Solen plans, forecasts, measures, and makes decisions across our portfolio of 20+ software companies and the holding company. Reporting to the CFO, this role partners as a peer with the Controller: the Controller owns the close, books, and consolidated actuals, while the Director of FP&A owns the budget, forecast, KPIs, Monthly Business Review, and the models behind capital allocation and acquisitions.

This is a build-as-you-go role. Our businesses run with real autonomy and span recurring SaaS, usage-based fees, professional services, and hardware. You will design the planning and reporting engine that replaces today's manual, company-by-company reporting, build the team that runs it, and support the CFO in raising debt and equity capital.

Key Responsibilities

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

Own the annual budget, quarterly re-forecast, rolling forecast, and long-range plan across all OpCos and the HoldCo, with one planning calendar and standard templates.
Build driver-based models suited to each revenue model: ARR, retention and churn cohorts, usage volumes, utilization and billable hours, hardware and license sales, and headcount.
Produce a consolidated, scenario-ready outlook for the CFO, CEO, and board.
Own forward cash forecasting and liquidity and covenant-headroom modelling in partnership with the Controller.
Track forecast accuracy, explain material misses, and continuously improve the process.

Portfolio Performance & KPIs

Define and deploy a consistent KPI framework across the portfolio, benchmarked against Solen's investment thesis.
Track unit economics, retention cohorts, customer profitability, and cost structure by function to benchmark OpCos against each other and best-in-class.
Support OpCo leaders on pricing, customer profitability, cost optimization, and financial turnarounds.

Monthly Business Review & Reporting

Own the MBR cadence, structure, KPI package, and follow-through on action items, raising the quality of insight in every review.
Partner with divisional controllers who run OpCo-level MBRs, equipping them with better data, tools, and insight.
Standardize and automate management reporting and dashboards in Power BI, and develop digital, real-time, and AI-native reporting.
Own the reporting roadmap, defining every metric once and building core reports such as the ARR bridge, budget-versus-actual, organic versus inorganic growth, EBITDA bridge, free cash flow, 13-week cash forecast, and return on invested capital.

Capital Allocation, Capital Raising & M&A

Build the models that guide capital allocation across reinvestment, bolt-on acquisitions, and cash returned to the HoldCo.
Support the CFO and deal team with acquisition models: valuation, diligence, pro formas, and synergy cases.
Support the CFO on debt and equity raises and refinancing with models, projections, scenario analysis, and lender and investor materials.
Track post-acquisition performance against the underwriting case and onboard new acquisitions into planning and KPIs from day one.

FP&A Team Build-Out

Design the FP&A operating model for a lean, decentralized portfolio.
Recruit, hire, and develop a best-in-class FP&A and business partner team.
Establish clear ownership between FP&A, the Controller, divisional controllers, and OpCo finance leaders.
Foster a culture of ownership, candor, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, accounting, or a related field; MBA or CFA preferred.
8+ years of progressive FP&A, corporate finance, or strategic finance experience.
Direct ownership of budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning for a multi-entity or decentralized business (e.g., PE-backed platform, roll-up, or multi-brand company).
Experience building, leading, and developing an FP&A or business partner team.
Excellent financial modelling skills, including driver-based forecasting and scenario analysis; advanced Excel.
Experience designing KPI frameworks and running recurring business reviews with operating leaders.
Experience building management reporting and dashboards in a BI tool.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations for a CEO, board, or non-finance operator.
Willing to work on-site in Salt Lake City or Park City, UT, or in New York, NY with regular travel to Utah, and occasional international travel to Lisbon, Portugal.
Legally authorized to work in the United States.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in B2B or vertical market SaaS, including ARR, GRR/NRR, and cohort analysis.
Experience modelling mixed revenue streams: subscription, usage-based, professional services, and hardware.
Background in private equity, permanent capital, investment banking, or Big-4 transaction advisory.
Experience supporting debt or equity raises or refinancing.
Experience using AI tools to automate manual finance work.
Working knowledge of Power BI and Sage Intacct or a comparable multi-entity ERP.
Experience with multi-currency planning and teams based outside the U.S.

Not every candidate will meet every requirement. If you have shown real trajectory and results, we encourage you to apply.

What Success Looks Like

One planning and forecasting engine is live across all OpCos and the HoldCo, with a full budget cycle and rolling forecast completed and forecast accuracy improving.
A consistent KPI framework is adopted by every OpCo, with each company viewed on one comparable scorecard against Solen's investment thesis.
The MBR runs on a predictable cadence with a standardized, automated package, and the highest-priority reports are live.
The FP&A function is defined, first hires are ramping, and manual reporting has come off the accounting team.
Capital allocation, acquisition, and financing models exist and have informed real decisions.
The CFO, CEO, Portfolio Leaders, and GMs seek FP&A's view before major decisions.

Solen-isms (How We Operate)

Ownership Mindset: We own the mission. We don't wait to be told. We lead, fix, and build as if it were ours. When problems arise, we run toward them, not away.
Benchmark to Best: We seek out excellence. We measure ourselves against the best and adapt quickly, always looking for the edge that moves us forward.
Openly Self-Critical: Leaders go first: they surface their misses early, ask for direct feedback, and turn “game film” into better decisions and better systems.
Disagree & Commit: Leaders disagree openly and constructively, regardless of title or tenure, because truth is how we avoid bureaucracy and benchmark to best.
Figureitoutiveness: Embracing challenges, fostering growth, and taking initiative, leaders thrive on hard work and high failure tolerance.
Mutual Elevation: Committed to growth, elevating teams, developing future leaders, and removing barriers to mastery and joy.
Learn-it-alls: Learn-it-alls, not know-it-alls, embracing failure as part of growth and progress.
Pioneering: Pioneering driven by opportunity, using first principles thinking and unbound by tradition or rules.
Will to Win: Leaders relentlessly pursue potential, reject mediocrity, and get what they tolerate.
Dialectical: We learn through conversation. We ask, listen, question, and evolve — valuing disagreement as a tool for alignment and deeper understanding.
Frugality: Achieving more with less, focusing on quality, long-term value, and company-wide responsibility.
Candor: We communicate with integrity, transparency, and respect in all conversations.
Kaizen: Kaizen is continuous improvement as a way of life. Leaders make hundreds of small upgrades that compound, turning lessons into standards and standards into durable systems.

Solen Software Group will never request payment, banking information, or other sensitive personal or financial details during any stage of the recruitment process. We take care of those dedicated to taking care of animals.

VetStrategy is Canada's leading veterinary network, with over 360 hospitals and clinics and more than 5,500 veterinary professionals across the country. As part of IVC Evidensia, we support veterinary teams with the resources, expertise and operational leadership they need to deliver exceptional care and build thriving practices.

We are seeking an experienced and strategic Operations Director. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in operations management, exceptional leadership skills, and a proven track record of successfully managing multiple locations. The Operations Director works closely with Regional Medical Directors and corporate leaders to consistent delivery of best-in-class care, ensuring our practices embody and operate in alignment with VetStrategy’s values and Leadership Behaviours.

Greater Toronto Area, ON. This is a regionally based role requiring regular travel across assigned veterinary practices. Flexibility to work remotely when not required on-site.

About the Town of Lynn Lake, Manitoba

Surrounded by boreal forest, pristine northern lakes, and located 1,076 km northwest of Winnipeg, Lynn Lake has a population of about 600 people and offers a unique northern lifestyle with exceptional fishing, hunting, hiking, canoeing, and extensive ATV and snowmobile trails. Local amenities include West Lynn Heights School (K–12), the Lynn Lake Hospital and Clinic, RCMP Detachment, Regional Conservation Office, and an arena offering year-round programming, a fully equipped fitness centre, and all-weather roads and highways.

For a municipal administrator seeking meaningful impact, Lynn Lake offers a rare opportunity to help guide a northern community through a period of renewal, growth, and long-term sustainability. A major gold mining project is expected to bring renewed economic activity, new residents, and long-term growth opportunities for the municipality. This represents a pivotal moment in Lynn Lake’s history as the community transitions toward a time of revitalization and sustainable development.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to Mayor and Council, the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) is the senior administrative leader of the municipality, responsible for the effective and efficient administration of the Town of Lynn Lake. The CAO will provide strategic advice and operational leadership across all municipal functions, including administration, financial management, human resources, economic development, programs, and services. The successful candidate will be a diplomatic, results-oriented, leader with strong financial acumen, sound judgment, and the ability to build collaborative relationships with Council, staff, community members, Indigenous partners, and regional stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role requiring an approachable, relationship-driven, adaptable, and future-minded municipal leader committed to a northern lifestyle. This role offers a comprehensive overall total compensation package that includes furnished municipal housing, relocation assistance, northern retention bonus, benefits and pension.

Key Responsibilities

Administer the business affairs of the municipality in accordance with the Municipal Act and other statutes of the province.
Function as an effective liaison between the Council, staff, community, Indigenous groups, industry, regional and government partners.
Provide strategic advice to Mayor and Council on governance, legislation, policy, community priorities, and long-term strategic direction.
Advance community and economic development by negotiating agreements, managing mining-related and infrastructure impacts, securing funding, and supporting strategic growth opportunities –including grant opportunities for infrastructure and capital projects.
Lead the effective delivery of municipal administration, programs, services, infrastructure, and capital projects, ensuring Council decisions are implemented and residents receive responsive service.
Strengthen organizational effectiveness, transparency, and risk management through clear communication, modern administrative and digital systems, information security, records management, and process improvement.
Oversee operating and capital budgets, financial reporting, internal controls, audits, taxation, procurement, grants, borrowing, and long-term financial and asset-management planning.
Responsible for all human resource functions, including effective recruitment, employee development, performance management, labour relations, workplace safety, team engagement, and organizational culture initiatives.
Provide supportive leadership and direction to staff and management, fostering an approach focused on collaboration, effective communication, mentorship, and development.
Play a pivotal role in promoting new investment and building the community during a time of opportunity and renewed growth.

Selection Criteria

Degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, or related discipline.
Completion of the Manitoba Municipal Administrators Certificate (CMMA), equivalent training, or willingness to obtain.
3-5 years senior management experience in a municipal environment; previous CAO experience is an asset.
Empowering leader with ability to manage stress in a dynamic and evolving environment.
Strong financial management and budgeting expertise, and willingness to learn municipal financial software (ASYST).
Knowledge of municipal governance, The Municipal Act and proven ability to work effectively with elected officials, staff, and the public.
Excellent public relations, interpersonal and communication skills, coupled with the ability to negotiate, influence, and facilitate.
Exceptional relationship building skills and ability to establish credibility and trust with a diverse group of people.
Demonstrated political acumen, visionary leader, and solid decision maker with a high level of ethics, values, and integrity.
Knowledge in computer systems for business applications and capacity to blend systems, people, and process to optimize operations.
Valid Class 5 Drivers License.
Assets include community or economic development experience, and experience working in northern, rural, or remote communities.

To apply submit a resume and cover letter detailing how you meet the position requirements.

new_jobs.description:
The Klick Group
—comprising Klick Health (including Klick Katalyst and btwelve), Klick Media Group, Klick Applied Sciences (including Klick Labs), Klick Consulting, and Klick Ventures—is an ecosystem dedicated to realizing the full potential of our people and clients in life sciences. Founded in 1997, we have offices in New York, Philadelphia, Saratoga Springs, Toronto, London, São Paulo, and Singapore. Consistently named a Best Managed Company, Most Admired Corporate Culture, and Great Place to Work, Klick is committed to fostering a high-performance, people-first culture with creativity, collaboration, innovation, and impact across everything we do.

About Our Technology Craft

The Technology Craft powers Klick’s platforms, products, and delivery capabilities across healthcare and life sciences. Teams design, build, and operate scalable, secure, and compliant solutions across web, CRM, data, and marketing technologies. By partnering closely with Strategy, Creative, and Client Services, the Technology Craft enables integrated omnichannel experiences that deliver real business impact.

Job Description

The Vice President, Technology (Technology Enablement) is accountable for the successful delivery of Klick’s core omnichannel technology solutions across a portfolio of healthcare and life sciences clients. Reporting to the SVP of Technology, this role provides portfolio-level delivery leadership, ensures consistent execution across teams, and builds client confidence in complex, regulated environments. The VP leads through senior Technology Enablement Leads, balancing delivery excellence, operational rigor, and scalable practices as client needs and platforms evolve.

What You’ll Do

Lead delivery execution across a multi-client technology portfolio spanning web platforms, CRM systems, Veeva, and integrated marketing technologies.
Own end-to-end accountability for technology delivery outcomes across Klick-hosted and client-managed environments, ensuring adherence to SDLC, quality, and regulatory requirements.
Partner with Client Services, Omnichannel Enablement, Strategy, Creative, PMO, and Technology leaders to align delivery plans with business and omnichannel objectives.
Act as the escalation point for delivery risk, making informed trade-offs across scope, resourcing, timing, and quality to maintain predictability and client confidence.
Evolve Klick’s technology delivery operating model by improving governance, forecasting, KPIs, and delivery standards to support scalable, repeatable execution.

Qualifications

Required:

12+ years of experience delivering complex enterprise technology solutions, with accountability for large-scale, multi-stream delivery programs.
Demonstrated leadership overseeing omnichannel technology delivery across platforms such as Salesforce, Veeva, Adobe Experience Manager, or comparable enterprise ecosystems.
Proven experience leading through senior delivery leaders and cross-functional teams, with clear ownership of outcomes across multiple concurrent initiatives.
Hands-on experience with delivery governance frameworks, including SDLC, portfolio planning, risk management, and delivery performance metrics.
Strong executive communication skills, including translating technical risk and delivery trade-offs for senior business, IT, and client stakeholders.

Desired:

Comfort and enthusiasm for using AI as a regular part of how work gets done.
Experience delivering technology solutions within US pharmaceutical or healthcare environments, including exposure to regulatory and MLR considerations.
Agency or consulting background supporting enterprise clients across multiple accounts and delivery models.
Experience contributing to growth and solution shaping efforts by assessing feasibility, delivery risk, and execution readiness.
Demonstrated success building and scaling delivery leadership teams while fostering continuous improvement and operational maturity.

Additional Information

This posting is to backfill a role at Klick.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

Klick is consciously creating a culture where everyone can thrive and grow in their careers. We believe that our best work comes from our diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We strongly encourage members of historically underrepresented communities to apply, including Black people, Indigenous peoples, and other people of color, people with disabilities, people from gender and sexually diverse communities and people with intersectional identities. We're also committed to developing an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment process and work environment. Should you require any accommodation, please contact us at careers@klick.com and we will work with you to meet your accessibility needs and ensure you have a positive experience.

WHO WE ARE 

Zeta Global (NYSE: ZETA) is the AI-Powered Marketing Cloud that leverages advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and trillions of consumer signals to make it easier for marketers to acquire, grow, and retain customers more efficiently. Through the Zeta Marketing Platform (ZMP), our vision is to make sophisticated marketing simple by unifying identity, intelligence, and omnichannel activation into a single platform – powered by one of the industry’s largest proprietary databases and AI. Our enterprise customers across multiple verticals are empowered to personalize experiences with consumers at an individual level across every channel, delivering better results for marketing programs. Zeta was founded in 2007 by David A. Steinberg and John Sculley and is headquartered in New York City with offices around the world. To learn more, go to www.zetaglobal.com.
THE ROLE 

We are looking for a highly motivated and organized Strategic Account Director to join our Client Experience team. In this critical role, you will act as the linchpin connecting presales strategy with post-sales execution, fostering collaboration across sales, customer success, data and analytics teams. You will leverage your expertise to build deep client relationships, deliver actionable insights, and develop strategic roadmaps to drive measurable outcomes. If you are motivated about using data to tell compelling performance stories and enhance marketing strategies, we want to hear from you.
This role is remote out of Toronto, Ontario in Canada.
RESPONSIBILITIES

Serve as the primary liaison across sales, customer success, data cloud, and analytics teams to ensure seamless strategy alignment and execution. 

Bridge presales strategy with post-sales execution, maintaining continuity of objectives and fostering collaboration. 

Develop and deliver forward-thinking strategic roadmaps that align with client goals and business outcomes. 

Provide actionable insights, trends, and opportunities from the Zeta Marketing Platform (ZMP) to inform and enhance client campaigns. 

Leverage ZMP Intelligence offerings. 

Build deep client relationships, acting as a trusted advisor and advocate for their business objectives. 

Facilitate collaborative client sessions, to drive innovation and alignment. 

Collaborate internally to ensure successful onboarding and activation of first-party (1P) data, leveraging audience intelligence to optimize campaigns. 

Monitor and manage roadmap deliverables, clarifying objectives, defining tasks, and ensuring timely delivery. 

Identify risks and opportunities in client strategies, proposing innovative solutions to optimize performance. 

Write and share reports that clearly and strongly explain progress, insights, and suggestions. 

Qualifications:

8+ years of experience in strategic account management, marketing strategy, or related roles. 

Proven expertise in leveraging first-party (1P) data for marketing insights, personalization, and activation. 

Solid knowledge of cross-channel marketing, including digital, media, and traditional channels. 

Paid digital media experience within retail, CPG, pharma, finance and travel industries preferable.

Exceptional collaboration and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and align diverse teams. 

Exemplary analytical skills, with a track record of using data to inform strategy and storytelling. 

Outstanding communication and presentation skills, with experience in delivering strategic roadmaps and performance stories to senior stakeholders. 

An initiative-taking, problem-solving mindset and an interest for leading innovation and performance. 

Bachelor’s degree in marketing, Business, or related field (MBA preferred).

Unlimited PTO 

Excellent medical, dental, and vision coverage 

Employee Equity 

Employee Discounts, Virtual Wellness Classes, and Pet Insurance And more!!

CAD, depending on location and experience.
